w: Swamishri visits meeting place of Lord Swaminarayan and Bishop Heber, Nadiad.
Parents Meet at the Akshar Purushottam Hostel, Nadiad.
After his morning puja, Swamishri performed pujan of bricks for the foundation of a Hari mandir in the village of Vadadla .
Senior sadhus performed the murti pratishtha and inaugurated the newly built Swaminarayan Mandir in the village of Bhatpura.

Sixty-one satsangi balaks, kishores and sanchalaks from E. Africa and S. Africa had been reciting bhajans, shloks and Swamini Vato for the last three days during Swamishri's walking and lunch sessions. Some had also delivered speeches in Gujarati and English. Today, at 11.00 a.m., Swamishri addressed them in a special assembly. Swamishri appreciated and congratulated them for their presentations and steadfastness in observing satsang disciplines. In his blessings, Swamishri emphasized that they should all focus on their studies and put efforts on a regular basis. He added that regular devotion to God and attendance to the weekly satsang assembly was imperative for their moral and spiritual development.

After Viveksagar Swami’s exposition, Dr Swami discoursed on the subject of ‘Thought’. Thereafter the youths presented a speech and a street play depicting today’s youth. Then a youth asked Swamishri as to how they could stay aloof from the decadent situation. Swamishri replied, “Whatever that dislodges one from character, bhajan, bhakti and spirituality is kusang (bad company). If you want to be virtuous then you must exercise discrimination in watching television. Peace can only be attained through God and His Sadhu. Through them one is redeemed off bad qualities. One should not drink and gamble. Earn money through honest ways. If one progresses through wrong means then one will not have love for God and His Sadhu. By having refuge in God one must cultivate good thoughts study well, serve the country and strive for redeeming one’s atma.”

A veteran devotee’s son used to attend satsang and visit mandir for darshan. But because of tension due to his worldly duties he had taken to drinking. Gradually, because of this habit his frequency in attending the weekly Satsang assembly diminished. Today, he had come for Swamishri’s darshan. Swamishri lovingly explained to him, “First you must give up drinking. Be strong. Your tension cannot be resolved through drinking. Pray, offer bhakti, do satsang and seva and your tension will go away.” Swamishri reinstated satsang in the youth through four means.

When some tension came into a youth's life through his worldly responsibilities, he took to the bad habit of drinking alcohol, and because of it he gradually drifted away from satsang. Today he had come for the darshan of Pramukh Swami Maharaj. Lovingly explaining to him, Swamishri said, "First of all, stop drinking. Keep up your strength. Tension does not reduce with alcohol. Pray, offer devotion, do satsang, do seva. That will reduce tension."
Swamishri showed him four ways to reduce tension, four alternatives to alcohol, and explaining with affection, turned him to the path of satsang.

Ramanbhai, Khodabhai, Thakorbhai Gohil, Kaushikbhai Patel and Lakshminarayan Yogi, who offer their services at Swaminarayan Akshardham, cycled from New Delhi to celebrate the BAPS Centenary Celebrations.

This is the first morning in Mumbai. Today is also a Sunday. From the thirteenth floor, the sea can be seen clearly on both sides. Of course, the misty atmosphere of the early morning is an obstacle, but as the sun rises higher, the curtain of mist lifts from over Mumbai. Here, until Pramukh Swami Maharaj's health check is done, almost all programmes have been suspended.

Swamishri finished his morning routine at 8.00 and came out of his room. The soft rays coming from the east were the first to perform abhishek on Swamishri's divine body. Swamishri came down by the big lift to the mandir on the ground floor for darshan of Thakorji. First he went to Akshar Bhuvan opposite for the abhishek darshan of Nilkanth Varni. Casting his glance on the devotees sitting here, Swamishri came to the domed part of the mandir. Here too all those sitting received the benefit of Swamishri's darshan peacefully. After darshan of Hanumanji and Ganpatiji, Swamishri got up from the wheelchair. After darshan of Ghanshyam Maharaj, Swamishri's eyes went to the devotees sitting on the right. Swamishri began walking that way, and Narayancharan Swami said, "Only these same devotees are sitting there. They have had your darshan from here."
Swamishri said, "I want to go there."

This pull Swamishri felt towards the devotees was his affection, his wish to please everyone. On the other hand, there was also the limitation of his age and health. That is why, in the end, Swamishri went there seated in the wheelchair, and only when he had given darshan to the devotees sitting towards the new book stall and along the circumambulation was he satisfied.
Every moment, Swamishri is eager to please everyone, because he is loving to his devotees.

ds.t: Hold my hand to the end
w: Keeping Pramukh Swami Maharaj's present health in mind, Swamishri is given an injection at 10.00 in the morning. Now Dr Kiranbhai Doshi came to give Swamishri the injection, and Dr Nikul was with him. He was holding Swamishri's hand. Dr Nikul said, "Bapa! Keep holding my hand like this right to the end."
Swamishri said, "That depends on your faith; the basic conviction should never waver."
Then Dr Nikul said, "Bapa! When something like this happens to your health, Kiranbhai worries a lot."

Swamishri said, "What is there to worry about in that? Nothing will happen; one will just go and sit in God's abode." Swamishri spoke with complete freedom from worry, in carefree joy. That was Swamishri's realisation of the self.

At 11.30 he was to get up to go and rest. After looking at the clock, Pramukh Swami Maharaj said, "What is there to rest?" Saying this, he burst out laughing. For Swamishri, constant devotion to work full of seva is itself health and rest.
Today, during the meetings, the resident editor of the newspaper "Sandesh" in Surat came to meet Mahant Swami Maharaj. He asked Swamishri, "What is India's future like?"
"It is good, and it will become (even better)." It was as if prophetic words fell from Swamishri's lips!

ds.t: Do it properly or not at all
w: This evening, as Mahant Swami Maharaj was eating fruit, Shrutiprakashdas Swami was giving information about the patotsav ceremony to be held tomorrow for the 20th anniversary celebration of the Surat mandir. Hearing it, Swamishri was pleased with the care and precision the sadhus had taken in the rituals, and stating his life principle, he said, "If you do something, do it properly; otherwise do not do it."
Swamishri insists on perfection in work. With him, the attitude of "it will do" does not work.

Today was Satsang Day, in which Mahant Swami Maharaj was asked, "To become a doctor one needs a doctor; in the same way, to become brahmarup one needs Brahma. Such a Brahma, Pramukh Swamiji Maharaj, has placed our hand in yours, so you are Aksharbrahman."
Swamishri laughed a little and said, "Everyone knows."
The whole assembly was filled with the sound of applause.
Today at the evening meal Mahant Swami Maharaj said, "Today (in the assembly) Dharmaprakash Swami's name did not come up."

What had happened was that today in the assembly various sadhus had come forward to garland him, and among them Dharmaprakashdas Swami's name had been left out. Swamishri did not like this at all, because from 1983, for the first 18 years, he had travelled in this region with great effort.
The attendant sadhus said, "Once the meal is finished, let us call him."
But Swamishri expressed the wish, "Call him right now."

Dharmaprakashdas Swami was called. While still eating, Swamishri undid with his left hand the sacred thread that had been tied on his right wrist at today's guru puja, and then, wiping his right hand, tied the thread on Dharmaprakashdas Swami's wrist himself. He also gave him prasad from his thal and said, "In the beginning we travelled together a lot."
The organising sadhus too apologised to Swamishri, saying, "Swami! We made a mistake."
Swamishri said to Dharmaprakashdas Swami, "You were not getting permission, then you went to meet your father in hospital and you got permission!"
The sadhus asked Dharmaprakashdas Swami, "When was this?"
He said, "1975, Mumbai. I got permission after a seven year struggle."
But the remarkable thing was how exactly Swamishri remembers even something from 42 years ago!
How much is stored like this in Swamishri's treasure chest of memories!!

st.t: Mayor of London, Sadiq Khan Visits Swaminarayan Akshardham, New Delhi
w: Mayor of London, Sadiq Khan, visited Swaminarayan Akshardham in New Delhi to experience India’s beauty, culture and values.

On behalf of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj (spiritual head of Swaminarayan Akshardham and BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha), senior sadhus traditionally welcomed Mayor Sadiq Khan and delegation with a garland of flowers, tilaka (vermillion powder) and the tying of the sacred kalva (sacred thread).

After admiring the Mayur Dwar (Peacock Gate), Mayor Khan visited the Swaminarayan Akshardham Mandir where he witnessed the world’s ‘Largest Comprehensive Hindu Temple’. He offered his respects and admired the Mandir’s art and architecture.
Mayor Sadiq Khan visited the Gajendra Pithika (Elephant Plinth) that includes 148 life-sized carved stone elephants depicting message of social harmony, peace and spirituality.

With prayers for world peace and harmony, Mayor Khan offered ‘abhishek’, the ceremonial pouring of sanctified water from 151 holy rivers, lakes and ponds across India on the sacred image of Shri Neelkanth Varni.

Thereafter, Mayor Khan experienced the educational exhibition Sanskruti Vihar – a cultural voyage that sails through 10,000 years of India’s glorious heritage, highlighting India’s contributions to humanity through the ages.

Sharing his sentiments at Akshardham, Mayor of London Sadiq Khan wrote, “Jay Swaminarayan. Thank you so much for your hospitality, friendship, warmth and sharing your knowledge. It is humbling to visit Akshardham. I leave with fond memories.”
